articles.title: British South Asians in Football: How 2024 became another landmark year in the English game
articles.summary: Sky Sports News looks back on another unforgettable year for British South Asians in football where records were broken, league titles were won, landmarks were reached, and promotions were clinched
articles.body:
Records were broken, league titles were won, landmarks were reached, and promotions were clinched.

There were significant developments away from the pitch, with a number of British South Asians also earning the opportunity to play on the international stage.

Sky Sports News had it covered from all angles - we look back at an unforgettable year for British South Asians in football…

There were fireworks at the start of the year with Kick it Out chair Sanjay Bhandari MBE hitting out at "lazy racist stereotyping" after a now-deleted LinkedIn post by a Crystal Palace academy scout who dismissed the community's under-representation from elite football as simply being down to Asian families putting "all their efforts into education", adding they were "more aligned to the game of cricket".

But the focus was quickly back on the football when Luton Town earned almost £50,000 from their Women's FA Cup run after veteran forward Sam Khan's winner against Keynsham Town set up a fourth-round tie against WSL side Brighton.

With the January transfer window open, Sky Sports News exclusively revealed Birmingham City teenager Brandon Khela was set to join Ross County on loan for the rest of the season.

The midfielder went on to earn his first taste of top-division football and make his first-ever league start in Ross County's historic Scottish Premiership clash away at Celtic.

There was also a moment of Africa Cup of Nations history to savour, when Tarryn Allarakhia - who has mixed Indian and East African heritage - turned out for Tanzania and became the first British South Asian ever to play at a Cup of Nations in the modern era.

Former Spurs youngster Zahmena Malik clinched a move to Saudi Arabian women's side Al Hmmah, while Arjan Raikhy came on to replace Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and make his Championship debut for Leicester City.

There was another breakthrough moment when trailblazer Sunny Singh Gill became the first British South Asian ever to referee a Premier League game as he presided over Crystal Palace's clash with Luton Town at Selhurst Park.

At the turn of 2024, Sky Sports News broke the news that Sunny's brother Bhupinder was going to make history as the first Sikh-Punjabi assistant referee to officiate in the Premier League.

There was also an unforgettable moment for Blues teenager Riya Mannu, who featured in a Women's Championship game away at Reading, becoming the first British South Asian ever to play league football for Birmingham City Women.

Speaking to Sky Sports News moments after the final whistle, Mannu's mother said: "We knew this day would come because Riya is really persistent and so determined.

"But to actually see her do it was just mind-blowing. Riya's been working towards this moment for such a long time and Blues have been amazing since day one."

In an exclusive interview with Sky Football the following month, Dhanda once again stepped up for British South Asians in Football , speaking up about the uphill battle against unconscious bias the community continues to face in the elite game.

The Football Association conceded the under-representation of South Asians in the game is "stark" and could be viewed as "a football emergency", adding that taking steps to addressing the issue is now "a long-term aim" for English football's governing body.

The FA is now expected to deliver its first dedicated South Asians in Football plan early in 2025.

Millie Chandarana was at it again as she helped Blackburn Rovers to a record Women's Championship points total, while also landing her team's Goal of the Season for the second year in a row after her wonder-strike against Charlton.

Kira Rai also enjoyed a stunning end to the campaign, becoming the first British South Asian ever to win a national trophy with Derby County as the Ewe Rams clinched the FA National Plate.

Hamza Choudhury helped Leicester City win the Championship title and earn promotion back to the Premier League under now-Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca.

Dhanda and Khela also enjoyed a thrilling end to the season as they helped Ross County emerge victorious from the relegation play-off, preserving the club's status in the Scottish Premiership.

Khela scored the first goal of his senior career in that game to end his loan adventure in Scotland on a high.

Singh's performances earned him his first appearance in the annual South Asians in Football Team of the Season - with Chandarana, Choudhury and Dhanda all retaining their places from the previous season.

The team was showcased at Brentford's Gtech Community Stadium, and at Leicester City, before going on show at the home of English football at the Asian Football Awards at Wembley Stadium later in the year.

Dhanda's stunning two-year spell at Ross County earned him a big move to Scottish Premiership giants Hearts following the expiry of his contract.

In the English Championship, Danny Batth joined Blackburn Rovers, with Sky Sports News revealing that goalkeeper Rohan Luthra was joining Derby County after leaving Cardiff City.

Elsewhere, Dilan Markanday joined Chesterfield on loan from Blackburn, Wolves academy graduate Kam Kandola signed for Kidderminster Harriers, Dillon De Silva moved to Sutton United and Tarryn Allarakhia joined Rochdale.

Former England youth international Asmita Ale joined WSL side Leicester City on a permanent basis following her loan from Spurs the previous season.

Chandarana left Blackburn Rovers to join ambitious Nottingham Forest. Birmingham City's Layla Banaras returned to Wolves on a dual registration and Zahmena Malik rejoined London Seaward.

Rai enjoyed a dream start to the new season, bringing up a century of career first-team appearances in a Derby shirt, having first joined the club as an U10s player.

Back at Birmingham for the 2024/25 season, Khela properly announced himself to the Blues fanbase with a sensational long-range winner in a League Cup tie at Charlton that was named best goal in the first round of the competition.

Barnsley midfielder Vimal Yoganathan scored the first goals of his senior career, netting both of the Tykes' goals in a 3-2 EFL trophy loss to Manchester United's youngsters in the EFL Trophy.

Shadab Iftikhar joined Shaun Maloney's staff as first-team coach at Wigan - marking a return to where his football journey started some years back, shadowing former Latics boss Roberto Martinez and providing opposition match analysis.

Elsewhere, Pav Singh replaced former Jamaica international Clayton Donaldson as manager of National League North side Farsley Celtic, becoming the highest-ranked British South Asian in such a role in English men's football.

Dhanda and Choudhury were named joint winners of the men's footballer of the year at the Asian Football Awards, with Rai named women's footballer of the year at the showpiece gala at Wembley Stadium. FC Utrecht midfielder Zidane Iqbal was named young player of the year as the awards returned after a seven-year absence.

There was a sharp dose of reality to come for South Asians in The Game, however, when a racist comment from the crowd was directed at assistant referee Bhupinder Singh Gill during Portsmouth's 1-1 draw with Oxford United at Fratton Park.

But Markanday's excellent form on loan at Chesterfield and Sonny Perkins' goal on his first league start for Leyton Orient provided cause for optimism towards the end of the year.

Perkins, who joined Orient on a season-long from Leeds United, also came on and scored with his first touch in Orient's 3-0 Boxing Day win at home to Blackpool.

Four British girls - Zahmena Malik, Nadia Khan, Amina Hanif and Sanah Mehdi - would all enjoy a 2024 to remember, representing Pakistan at the South Asian Football Federation Championship (SAFF) and helping the nation end the year with their highest-ever FIFA rankings points total.

Rovers defender Batth made his 500th senior first-team appearance, while fellow stalwart Mal Benning scored one of the most remarkable goals in English football in 2024, netting directly from a 60-yard free-kick in his own half in Shrewsbury Town's League One clash with Blackpool.

Ronan Maher, who joined Tamworth on loan from Walsall, also impressed as the year drew to a close, scoring an extra-time equaliser in an FA Cup second round to against Burton Albion. Goalkeeper Jaz Singh would then go on to save two penalties to seal Tamworth's progress to the third round and set up a dream third-round tie against Ange Postecoglou's Tottenham Hotspur in January.

articles.title: Football Association unveils first-ever South Asians in Football plan
articles.summary: Football Association releases first-ever South Asians in Football plan: "South Asians make up the largest minority group in England, and we want to build on great progress in recent years to grow representation across key areas of our game, including playing, coaching and refereeing."
articles.body:
'Build, Connect, Support' is the first plan from the national governing body for English football, focused specifically on making the Beautiful Game more accessible to the single-largest minority ethnic group in England.

Football has come under pressure in recent years to take meaningful action to address the severe under-representation of South Asians in the English game - with latest figures indicating that less than one per cent of professionally contracted players in this country hail from the community.

Sky Sports has stepped up and demonstrated leadership in this space by creating the first index page dedicated to British South Asians in Football in the history of mainstream media. The groundbreaking work represents the longest-running major initiative in the space, with Sky's contribution to South Asians in Football recognised with the inaugural Diversity in Media Award at the Asian Media Awards.

The Professional Footballers Association have since launched the AIMS project, with the Premier League later releasing a South Asian Action Plan, back in 2022.

The FA's plan comes following collaboration over the last 12 months with a number of key stakeholders across the game, in addition to organisations from across English football including the Premier League, EFL, Kick It Out, Football Supporters' Association, PFA and PGMOL (Professional Game Match Officials Ltd).

"Through our new 'Build, Connect, Support' plan, we aim to ensure that South Asian communities across the country have an increased awareness of - and access to - opportunities within our game," FA's head of diversity chief Dal Darroch.

"South Asians make up the largest minority group in England, and we want to build on great progress in recent years to grow representation across key areas of our game, including playing, coaching and refereeing.

"We're committed to continuing our close work with South Asian communities to ensure that our game is better reflective of our modern society, and this plan will bring a clear focus to our work in this area for the next three years."

The FA has set a range of different targets in the plan for various aspects of the game, including ambitious recruitment targets for refereeing, as well as dedicating slots on FA talent identification courses.

The national governing body is also implementing a grassroots football parents support network and is creating a scheme of work linking grassroots and community clubs with clubs higher up the football pyramid.

Separately, the FA will implement a bespoke scheme aimed at bringing professional clubs closer to South Asian communities locally and nationally.

The FA South Asian Shield - to be hosted at St George's Park - will see South Asian heritage clubs playing in non-league football compete in an annual tournament in coming seasons. The FA is also working on developing a dedicated South Asians in Football online platform.

Earlier this week, Hamza Choudhury - who is one of the highest-profile British South Asians in the English game - dropped down from the Premier League to join promotion-chasing Championship side Sheffield United on an initial loan deal.

articles.title: British South Asians in football: Who makes it into the 2024/25 team of the season?
articles.summary: Sky Sports News' Dev Trehan and Desi Ballers founder Zohaib Rashid pick the third annual combined XI, celebrating the on-field contribution made by British South Asians in football during the 2024/2025 season
articles.body:
Players from the community featured across the leagues in men's football and at every level of the English women's football pyramid, barring the Women's Championship.

Six players retain their places from last year but how does the 2024/25 team shape up?

Sky Sports journalist and FA Level 2 scout Dev Trehan sat down with Desi Ballers founder Zohaib Rashid to pick the third annual South Asians in football team of the season.

Jasbir Singh was in sparkling form for Tamworth, helping the Lambs to a top-half finish on their return to the National League following promotion last summer.

Singh was also on song in the FA Cup, saving two penalties against Burton Albion to set up a dream third-round tie at home to Tottenham, who needed extra time to earn victory and eventually progress.

Asmita Ale has enjoyed another stellar campaign in the Women's Super League, earning the full-back her third straight South Asians in football team of the season appearance.

Former England youth international Ale featured in 17 of Leicester City's 21 league matches so far this term, contributing three assists.

Mal Benning was one of Shrewsbury Town's most consistent performers during a difficult campaign. The left-back played 44 games in a season where he racked up both his 150th League One appearance and his 400th senior career appearance. Benning also scored on the final day of the season against Crawley.

Kam Kandola made his breakthrough in senior football following his departure from Wolves last summer after more than a decade with the Premier League club. Kandola played 30 games at the heart of the defence for Kidderminster Harriers, helping the club finish third in the National League North and qualify for the play-offs.

Danny Batth's undeniable influence at Blackburn Rovers sees him captain the 2024/25 South Asians in football team of the season. Batth made 37 league appearances during Rovers' push for the Championship play-offs, with the defender also playing in the 500th game of his career in December's 1-0 win against Hull City.

Millie Chandarana had an incredible season at Nottingham Forest, landing the first trophy of her senior career as they lifted the FA Women's National League Cup.

Chandarana also helped the team finish the league season unbeaten as Forest won the title and gained promotion to the Women's Championship as Invincibles .

Zidane Iqbal continued his progress at FC Utrecht, making 21 appearances in all competitions for the Eredivisie side and scoring a memorable goal in a 3-1 win at Almere City.

Iqbal, whose father is British-Pakistani, also made six international appearances for Iraq, turning out in World Cup qualifying and at the Arabian Gulf Cup.

Hamza Choudhury has become an integral part of Sheffield United's promotion-chasing side following his January loan move from Leicester City. A memorable campaign for the ex-England U21 midfielder has also seen him become the first top-flight player from this country to play international football for Bangladesh.

Dilan Markanday has come of age this season. The Blackburn Rovers attacking midfielder has scored 10 goals and contributing four assists across loan spells with League One Leyton Orient - and at League Two Chesterfield during the first half of the season - helping both teams reach the play-offs.

Brandon Khela started the season by scoring a worldie for Birmingham City in their 1-0 Carabao Cup win over Charlton Athletic. He ended it with a promotion winner's medal to end his loan at Bradford City as they went up to League One with an added-time winner against Fleetwood Town on the final day of the season.

Simran Jhamat bagged 11 goals for West Bromwich Albion Women, matching her tally from last season. Jhamat also won the first trophy of her senior career, getting on the scoresheet to wrap up a 6-2 victory over her former club Rugby Borough to help West Brom win the Birmingham County FA Challenge Cup.

articles.title: Nations League: How does it work and who is in each league
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains how the Uefa Nations League works ahead of the start of the 2026-27 competition
articles.body:
The 2026-27 Uefa Nations League campaign starts on Thursday.

The competition began in 2018, and the format sees each nation compete across four different divisions.

Each side competes for promotion and relegation in every campaign, with the best-performing nations in the top league going on to reach the play-offs at the end of each campaign.

The best-performing nations in each Nations League campaign can also strengthen their chances of qualifying for World Cups and European Championships, but cannot directly qualify for major tournaments through the Nations League alone.

Of the four leagues, teams are split into smaller groups. Leagues A, B and C are split into four groups of four, while League D contains only six teams.

Uefa also operates a Nations League in international women's football using a similar format.

How do the Uefa Nations League fixtures and format work?

Between September and November, each team in the Nations League will face every other team in their group twice; once at home and once away.

In League A, the top two teams from each group will make the quarter-finals later in that campaign. A knockout tournament between those eight teams will then play out to determine the overall Nations League winner.

In Leagues B, C and D, each group winner will be promoted up one league.

The teams finishing bottom of their groups in Leagues A, B and C will be relegated down one league.

Teams finishing second in groups from Leagues B, C and D will enter play-offs against teams that finish third in Leagues A, B and C in relegation play-offs.

The March international break in 2027 will see the quarter-finals from League A and the relegation play-offs between League A/B and League B/C take place.

The semi-finals and final for the Nations League campaign will take place in the international break of June 2027, as will the League C/D play-off.

The best-performing teams in the Nations League that do not qualify for the 2028 European Championships from the qualification campaign will enter into play-offs to earn the final qualifying spots for the tournament.

Group A1 : France, Italy, Belgium, Turkey

Group A2 : Germany, Netherlands, Serbia, Greece

Group A3 : Spain, Croatia, England, Czech Republic

Group A4 : Portugal, Denmark, Norway, Wales

Group B1 : Scotland, Switzerland, Slovenia, North Macedonia

Group B2 : Hungary, Ukraine, Georgia, Northern Ireland

Group B3 : Israel, Austria, Republic of Ireland, Kosovo

Group B4 : Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Romania, Sweden

Group C1 : Albania, Finland, Belarus, San Marino

Group C2 : Montenegro, Armenia, Cyprus, Latvia

Group C3 : Kazakhstan, Slovakia, Faroe Islands, Moldova

Group C4 : Iceland, Bulgaria, Estonia, Luxembourg

Group D2 : Lithuania, Azerbaijan, Liechtenstein

Are there Nations League campaigns in other continents?

There are also Nations League competitions played in the Asian and North and Central American continents.

South America do not currently have their own men's Nations League, but reports in late 2025 suggested their football confederation CONMEBOL may be considering launching their own equivalent. There is however a South American Nations League in women's football.

Africa and Oceania, the other continental confederations, do not have a Nations League competition.

articles.title: Max Dowman: Mikel Arteta admits 16-year-old Arsenal wonderkid could go out on loan in the future
articles.summary: Max Dowman impressed in Arsenal's win over Ipswich, underlying his position as one of the best young players in the game; the 16-year-old could be sent out on loan - he has only played one game this season; Mikel Arteta: "We have to be open, but now the focus is to be here."
articles.body:
Dowman continued his rise by starting and scoring twice in Arsenal's Carabao Cup win over Ipswich this week. After the game, Gunners midfielder Mikel Merino compared the young teenager to Barcelona and Spain star Lamine Yamal.

But those 90 minutes at Portman Road have been Dowman's only minutes of the season, and he did not make Arsenal's matchday squad in the wins over Aston Villa and Sunderland.

"We haven't really listened to any of the [loan] possibilities because we were clear that we want to have him in the squad, that we wanted him to be part of the pre-season," Arteta said.

"I'm going to start to see where we are from there. We will evaluate every six months where we are, what is the best thing for him to do and from there make the right decisions.

"It will depend on a lot of factors: what he needs, where the team is as well, the availability that we have in the squad, the amount of minutes that he's playing, the quality he's delivering when he's got those minutes.

"We have to be open, but now the focus is to be here and impact the team.

"There have been many cases of that age that they've gone [on loan] and they've been successful, some others not. Particularly, I think I was 17 when I went to Paris [Saint-Germain].

"Depending on the atmosphere that you find there, how much the coach believes in you, you go there just to be part of a squad, not to play minutes.

"Which country? Depends. But now he's in a great place. He's in a good place right now and let's keep him here."

Last season, Dowman became the Premier League's youngest goalscorer and starter in their title-winning campaign, as well as the youngest player in Champions League history, where they reached the final.

Over the last nine months, the Gunners have sent Ethan Nwaneri - who broke the record for the youngest ever Premier League player in 2022 at just 15 - out on loan to Marseille and Borussia Dortmund, where he is currently playing.

"Noni Madueke is not playing for Arsenal. For me, Max Dowman is better than Madueke now.

"If you're going to consider Madueke for England, then you definitely have to consider Dowman. And Dowman should be in that England squad right now. There's no doubt about that for me.

"He's going to be the future of England. He's 16 but this is his second season as a pro. Come the European Championships in 2028, he's going to be 18. He has to be in that squad and if he keeps doing what he's doing, he's going to be in that squad.

"What's the negative? If you're good enough, you're old enough. Professional players think a certain way. They're not thinking: I'm 16, I'll wait a few years. They're thinking I want to play right now, especially if they're thinking they're better than who's in there.

"Dowman needs to be considered, he's the future. The same as how Rio Ngumoha is the future, who is electric."

articles.title: Celtic: Martin O'Neill takes time to reflect, but where do Scottish Premiership champions go from here?
articles.summary: Celtic lost 1-0 to Rangers with their lead at top of Scottish Premiership cut to two points; it was their second Old Firm defeat inside a week; Martin O'Neill's side have suffered three straight defeats
articles.body:
The 74-year-old has already said he will stock and decide if it is "time to wrap it up" following the 1-0 loss to Rangers at Parkhead.

That defeat was their second against the Old Firm rivals inside a week that also saw them go down 3-1 to Ferencvaros in the Europa League.

Each display has been as concerning as the last, with the Hoops fans worried about what the rest of the season holds if nothing changes during the international break.

Celtic started the latest defence of their Scottish Premiership title with six straight wins, but at times they were unconvincing.

Their epic collapse in their Champions League play-off against LASK - from 4-0 up to crashing out 5-4 on aggregate - raised questions about O'Neill and his players.

A pasting last weekend against Rangers in the Scottish League Cup, followed by another abject display in the Europa League, saw the pressure increase.

Then came a 1-0 loss to their Old Firm rivals in front of 60,000 of their own fans.

They are still top of the top flight heading into a three-week international break, but it is a two-point gap rather than the commanding eight-point lead they could have had.

It is easy to point the finger at the manager when the results do not come, but Celtic's problems are bigger than that.

There were fan protests against the club's board last season and calls for change at the top have not gone away.

Questions have been asked about the quality and timing of the summer signings.

While record signing Kasper Hogh and Camilo Duran were brought in before their Champions League exit, the club then spent almost £20 on Mika Baur, Haissem Hassan and Joel van den Berg before Deadline Day.

O'Neill is still trying to find the best way to use them and his other five late signings in his team.

He has tried a series of different midfielders to no avail. He even dropped his wingers entirely in Sunday's Old Firm defeat, instead starting with five defenders and moving Kieran Tierney further forward. It was the same outcome.

Celtic have won 14 of the last 15 league titles without replacing some key players when they have been sold.

Some supporters feel domestic dominance has led to complacency from the board. But now there is a far stronger challenge from Rangers and Hearts.

Celtic have spent big this summer but many of them fear only a trophyless season will deliver their message that having vast money in the bank might not be more important than the right players on the pitch.

Things can turn quickly in Scottish football.

O'Neill returned to Celtic twice last season as interim manager and managed to steady the ship to deliver what had seemed an unlikely league and cup double.

The 74-year-old decided he was not ready to return to retirement and took over at Parkhead on a permanent basis, 21 years after his first spell came to an end.

The Irishman was a force to be reckoned with during his first spell at Parkhead when he delivered seven major trophies and a UEFA Cup final place in 2003.

He had a side hard to beat, which is the opposite of what can be levelled at them this season.

The Celtic supporters love Martin O'Neill, but even the most loyal are questioning whether it is time for him to walk away.

He made huge calls from the previous weekend's loss at Ibrox going into the clash with Ferencvaros in midweek.

They did not work. He made more changes for Rangers on Sunday and they also did not work.

He could still match last season's achievements. But if he cannot fix the big issues in his squad, he could be left with a trophyless season and a tarnished legacy.

With all the doom and gloom, it could be forgotten that Celtic are still top of the Scottish Premiership.

After Sunday's defeat to Rangers, O'Neill told Sky Sports he did not think "there's very much between the teams" and insisted "the history of the club proves it will fight back" from a week of turmoil.

He called for a bit of perspective, adding: "It's concerning. Is it a disaster? I don't think so. We have to rethink and reset."

He is right; the season is far from over.

They have played just seven of their 38 Premiership games and have another seven Europa League matches to play.

The current turmoil could still end in another season of success at Celtic.

articles.title: Valdano le reprocha a Valverde su reacción "naif" tras la entrada de roja de Kang-in Lee
articles.standfirst: "Acuérdate que con respecto a Valverde ya Mourinho le acusó en algún partido de naif, porque se había levantado demasiado pronto"
articles.summary: "Acuérdate que con respecto a Valverde ya Mourinho le acusó en algún partido de naif, porque se había levantado demasiado pronto"
articles.body: Jorge Valdano le comentó a Juanma Castaño la actitud "naif" de Fede Valverde en la polémica jugada con Kang-in Lee, en la que el VAR no llamó al árbitro Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias para que revisase una posible tarjeta roja al coreano por una plancha en el tobillo al uruguayo. "Acuérdate que con respecto a Valverde ya Mourinho le acusó en algún partido de naif, porque se había levantado demasiado pronto ante una falta que él creía que era merecedora de una sanción superior. Y aquí me da la sensación de que Valverde se levanta se levanta demasiado pronto, y eso puede inducir", explicó en Movistar Plus Deportes el que fuese jugador del Real Madrid de 1984 a 1987 y entrenador del equipo merengue de 1994 a 1996. La RAE informa que el término naif se "se usa para describir a alguien inocente, que confía con facilidad o que reacciona ante la vida con una sencillez parecida a la de un niño". Valdano se refería a las críticas de Mourinho tras el partido del Real Madrid contra el Real Betis, en las que el técnico luso dijo que "la primera jugada del partido es una tarjeta camarilla clara al jugador que ha golpeado a Valverde. Después, un minuto más tarde, otra amarilla para el jugador que ha hecho una falta importante a Vinicius… Pero los jugadores del Betis son más listos que los del Madrid, que son puros, naif. Los del Madrid se levantan inmediatamente, y los del Betis son más listos y, con el apoyo de una afición fantástica que empuja y presiona, consiguen este tipo de cosas". El Real Madrid informó que Valverde acabó lesionado el derbi contra el Atlético tras sufrir la dura entrada de Kang-in Lee: "Tras las pruebas realizadas a nuestro jugador Fede Valverde por los Servicios Médicos del Real Madrid se le ha diagnosticado un traumatismo severo en el tobillo izquierdo". Pablo González Fuertes, el analista arbitral del programa 'Marcador' de Radio MARCA, destacó que "la entrada de Kang-In Lee a Valverde pudo ser sancionada con roja". El que lo tenía claro era Mourinho, que se desató en rueda de prensa: "Sí, podíamos ahorrar la rueda de prensa porque la historia del partido está aquí. Son dos rojas claras (la de Kang-in Lee a Valverde y la del Cuti Romero a Bellingham)".

articles.title: Spygate: Southampton and Tonda Eckert await FA ruling
articles.summary: As Southampton manager Tonda Eckert awaits the FA hearing into his 'Spygate' misconduct conduct charge BBC sports editor Dan Roan speaks to him and club chief executive Phil Parsons on what happens next.
articles.body:
More than four months since the Spygate scandal erupted, Southampton manager Tonda Eckert's wait to discover his fate for authorising an espionage campaign is almost over.

This week, a decisive Football Association hearing is set to take place, after the German coach was charged with misconduct in July.

Spying on three clubs has already cost Southampton the chance of promotion to the Premier League (worth £200m), after they were expelled from the Championship play-off final. An EFL panel also docked the club four points for this season.

As the club prepared for the latest twist in the saga, BBC Sport spoke exclusively to both Eckert and Southampton chief executive Phil Parsons, who - in his first interview on the case - insists any further punishment would be "really tough to take".

But how are the club and their coach dealing with the prospect of more turmoil? What is at stake? And why have Southampton given a permanent role to the intern who was caught spying on Middlesbrough in May?

"I would lie if I say that the summer has just been easy. Of course, if you care deeply about your profession, about the football club, there's nothing that prepares you for that. There just isn't."

Eckert speaks slowly and with an intense gaze when asked to reflect on being at the centre of one of the biggest controversies in English football history.

The 33-year-old apologised in June after an EFL independent disciplinary commission found he had orchestrated a "contrived and determined plan" to spy on Oxford United, Ipswich Town, then Middlesbrough before the play-off semi-final.

Having insisted he was unaware it breached EFL rules, and that the spying had no impact on performances, Eckert was backed by Southampton.

His team have made an encouraging start to the new season. Without the four-point deduction, they would be fourth in the table, rather than 13th.

"We've talked a lot over the summer of how we want to go through that process of addressing everything, giving everyone the chance to put questions out that are still there, to put out what they feel and have gone through, and then also close the door and move on," he says.

"Because the reality is it's a new season. We have big ambitions as a football club, and in order to reach them, we need to move on."

That is easier said than done, with Eckert in limbo while he awaits the outcome of the FA's disciplinary process.

"I've had the chance to sit down and just talk the FA through everything that happened," he says. "And now it's up to them to make a decision. I don't really have any emotions towards that."

So does he feel the FA has listened to him during its investigation?

"That was my impression," he says. "We sat for almost four hours, so it's been quite a long conversation."

When asked whether he feels the club has been punished enough, and if a suspension for him would be excessive, Eckert chooses his words carefully.

"It's been a big, big punishment," he says. "Absolutely unheard of in the history of sports.

"And it's tough for me to say that because it concerns me. I'm judging on myself, not an outside situation. But I've asked for forgiveness for what I've done. I've apologised publicly.

"I think the punishment has been very hard on the club for the last season. And to go into a new season on minus four. And the rest is not for me to decide."

Southampton owner will not sack head coach Eckert

Parsons is more forthright on whether the club has been punished enough.

"We don't know what the FA will actually hand out," he says. "It could be a long ban. It could be a short ban. It could be a suspended sentence.

"What we hope as a club is they actually recognise where we are at the moment, and what we've already been through, because I think it has to be taken into account. I really feel like we've taken enough. We've been hurt. I think it's one of the largest sanctions ever when it comes to football, or even sporting, history.

"This isn't just about the club, this is about people. We lose money not being in the Premier League, but [local] businesses lose money. We had to spend a huge amount on legal fees, and it really impacts the club even further. We don't want to be seen as a victim of this. We need to get on. We've had our cards dealt."

When it is put to Parsons that the EFL's punishments applied to the club - rather than Eckert himself - he says: "I think it's impossible to sanction the manager without the club getting hurt even more."

The most recent precedent for this case came at the 2024 Olympics women's tournament, when Fifa banned Bev Priestman - Canada's head coach - from all football for a year, after opponents New Zealand were spied on.

Parsons insists "the Canadian case is very different" but if Eckert , who is only contracted until the end of the season, is also banned, how long would it have to be for the club to look elsewhere for a new coach?

"We don't know," he says, firmly denying having approached other coaches in case Eckert has to leave. Parsons also says the club may appeal if the ruling goes against them.

"We can't worry about something we can't control at the moment," he says. "We have to deal with it when we get there but we're hoping that they look at it sensibly."

Parsons says the club's ownership "want to back" Eckert.

"We've been through an entire transfer window when it comes to recruiting players for Tonda, and that's another challenge.

"We have to be looking at all scenarios. We've always spoken about any punishment being disproportionate...You're looking for fairness in approach. And have we had that treatment to us, from a disproportionate punishment? Well, I think a lot of people will view it that way. But do we want to sit there moaning about it? No.

"But it's going to be really tough to take if we get another punishment, on top of being thrown out of the play-offs, four points this season, and potentially more. So we're really hoping that the FA, the panel, are looking as this with a balanced view to what's already happened, because it's been really heavy."

When compared to the £10m fines that both the FA and Premier League handed Chelsea this year for making £47m in secret payments related to transfers across several seasons when they were owned by Roman Abramovich, some would agree Southampton have suffered enough.

Others however, would say the FA has little choice but to sanction Eckert.

After all, according to the EFL commission, the club employed "a particularly deplorable approach" by using junior members of staff to conduct the spying "at the direction of senior personnel".

An arbitration panel then detailed how a junior analyst intern said he felt under "extreme pressure".

Southampton's initial response to the crisis also contained "inaccuracies". Middlesbrough's head of football Kieran Scott said the club's behaviour had been "disgusting". , external

And when it is put to him that many expected Southampton to sack Eckert, and had they done so they would not be facing the current uncertainty, he replies: "Yeah, but Tonda also picked up the team in around 20th place in the Championship, and without him and his team we wouldn't have been in the play-off positions, and I think that deserves a bit of loyalty.

"OK, he has made a mistake and he's paid for that dearly. This has been really tough for him as a person already. I admire how strong he's been through this process because a lot of people could have cracked, the amount of pressure he was under."

For his part, Eckert says he is "very grateful for the support of the club because that could have been very different, and I think in most cases would have been very different".

The vast majority of Southampton fans that BBC Sport spoke to also seem to fully back the manager, something he says "means everything" to him.

Another to be supported is the intern involved - Will Salt - who was recently handed a permanent role as an analyst in the club's academy.

The scandal began when a photograph was published of Salt secretly filming Boro from behind a tree at their training ground before the play-off semi-final.

"He's been through a tough time," says Parsons.

"When your photo is put out to the public, that is something tough to deal with. A lot of people probably underestimated how that could have impacted a young lad so we've got a job to make sure that he's looked after in his early career. But he's a talented boy as well. I get good feedback and he's got a good role at the club."

Asked if reintegrating Salt had been challenging, given his allegations about the way he was treated, Parsons says: "I don't think Will said he felt under pressure directly from Tonda himself. He felt under pressure in the situation. And everybody knows in a job you can feel under pressure.

"But, yeah, I think Will's managed himself really well, and he'll grow from this."

So has the club learned its lessons? Parsons insists Eckert has studied the EFL's regulations, but also argues the rules could be clearer.

"They're very grey - that's something I'll continue to raise in EFL meetings," he says.

"But look, we've done something wrong, we'll get on with it."

Moving on is not easy, though. Last week, Wrexham's owners aimed a dig at Southampton by referencing the scandal in a social media advert before the two teams met. And during matches, rival fans regularly remind the club of the scandal.

"History is history and it'll be a part of our story going forwards," says Parsons. "It's about how we react now. It's given us a real togetherness and hopefully that continues through the season because we're stronger like that anyway.

"There's a bit of siege mentality as well, right - of 'everybody's against us', so we've got to embrace it."

The Championship has now paused until next month for the international break.

By the time Southampton next play - against local rivals Portsmouth on 11 October - Eckert should have learned his fate.

For now, however, his future remains uncertain.

articles.title: Álvaro Benito vislumbra un "problema más profundo" en el Madrid y distingue lo que no ve de Mourinho
articles.standfirst: "Si llevas dos años y pico viendo los mismos problemas sobre el terreno de juego... Entonces el problema es mucho más profundo. ¿No? Digo yo..."
articles.summary: "Si llevas dos años y pico viendo los mismos problemas sobre el terreno de juego... Entonces el problema es mucho más profundo. ¿No? Digo yo..."
articles.body: Álvaro Benito, futbolista del Real Madrid de 1995 a 2002 que se vio obligado a retirarse del fútbol en 2003 por culpa de las lesiones, compartió una "reflexión profunda" sobre el Real Madrid tras su derrota por 2-1 contra el Atlético de Madrid en el derbi madrileño. "Aquí la reflexión es mucho más profunda... Si llevas dos años y pico viendo los mismos problemas sobre el terreno de juego. La naturaleza de los problemas es exactamente la misma. No se atisba ningún cambio con ninguno de los entrenadores, siendo de diferente índole todos y cada uno... Entonces el problema es mucho más profundo. ¿No? Digo yo...", compartió el analista de 'Carrusel Deportivo' en la Cadena SER. El exfutbolista de 49 años subrayó que "se ven los mismos problemas desde hace más de dos años". Álvaro Benito, que lleva lustros triunfando en la música como vocalista del grupo Pignoise, destacó que "tú puedes ganar. Por ejemplo, el otro día en Elche ganas, pero la sensación que te da a nivel colectivo es que se reproducen los mismos problemas". "Todos podíamos barruntar que, salvo caso excepcional, hoy ibas a venir aquí (al Metropolitano) e ibas a ver lo que estamos viendo. Podías ganar o perder, pero yo no hablo de perder o ganar, porque al final el camino al resultado puede ir por diferentes lugares. Si expulsan al Cuti Romero en la primera parte hasta puedes hasta ganar el partido. Yo me refiero a la sensación colectiva, la idea de juego, qué propones, qué jugadores vas a poner en el once titular la mayoría de los días...", se explicó. Álvaro Benito también habló sobre el estilo que trata de implantar Mourinho en el Real Madrid y que no acaba de ver sobre el terreno de juego. "Mourinho... Históricamente bloque medio fortísimo, equipo corto, agresivo, robar y atacar vertical. ¡Perfecto! Eso le vendría perfecto al Real Madrid con las características de jugadores que tiene, pero es que no lo vemos", declaró el de Salamanca.

articles.title: The pros and cons of being a long-distance football manager
articles.summary: The pros and cons of being a long-distance football manager. Former Stoke City manager Tony Pulis talks to BBC Sport about how he managed teams despite keeping his family home hundreds of miles away.
articles.body:
Managing a football club is a tough job at the best of times.

There's the constant pressure to get results, impatience from fans and club owners, along with endless media scrutiny.

For some managers, there's the added complication of commuting from their family home - in some cases from hundreds of miles away.

Frank Lampard is one such example, with the Coventry manager choosing to split his time between the Midlands and London.

Jose Mourinho lived in a hotel during his time at Manchester United - dividing his time between a luxury five-star suite and his home - also in London.

It might come as a surprise to learn that Arne Slot chose to live in Hale, Greater Manchester while managing Liverpool - just down the road from Old Trafford, but about an hour's drive from Anfield.

Being close to Manchester airport made it easier for him to visit his wife and children, who remained in the Netherlands.

One of the longest commutes in the UK belonged to Tony Pulis. The former Stoke City manager kept his home on the south coast during his time in Staffordshire, which meant a round trip of more than 400 miles.

He travelled even further when he joined Middlesbrough in 2017, clocking up a massive 320 miles each way.

BBC Sport talked to Pulis about how he and other bosses like Lampard, Mourinho and Slot make it work.

'I never felt as if I was letting the club down'

Pulis explained how he spent most, if not all, of his working week near the clubs he managed, but drove back to his family home after games.

"My wife was absolutely adamant where we lived on the south coast was the place to bring our children up, and she was right," said the 68-year-old, who played for, and then managed, Bournemouth until 1994.

"I never felt as if I was letting the club down by having my family home away from where the club was.

"I actually felt that without having the family there, I spent more time thinking about and preparing for what I was doing.

"It's not very nice to say, but that way there's more space for you to do all those things you need to do as a manager.

"Clubs were always very good to me about my living arrangements during the week. For example, I had an apartment when I was at Stoke, which was lovely - I always stayed in nice places, which helped.

"It was always good because it meant wherever I was, my wife and children could come up and stay as well."

Pulis, who managed Stoke for 10 years in two different spells, added: "When I was at Stoke, I would drive home to the south coast after a game on the Saturday.

"It could take me three hours or more, but it was precious time because I could spend much of it on the phone and it is when I would start my preparation for our next match.

"My chairman Peter Coates would always speak to me then if we lost. If we'd won, he never bothered, knowing I wouldn't need comforting.

"Win or lose, however, I would always ring my assistants, David Kemp and Gerry Francis, and we would discuss the game in finer detail - away from the stadium to give us a different perspective.

"Then I would contact my chief scout, who would have been at our next opponent's game, for a quick run-down of what he had seen - their shape, patterns, strength, weaknesses and any injuries.

"By the time I arrived home, whatever our result, I would have my dinner on a tray in front of the TV while watching a recording of our opponent's last game, which I could get downloaded.

"Sunday was about spending all day with the family, but then either late on Sunday night or early on Monday morning I would be back up the motorway, with a clear view of what I believed was needed for our next game.

"There are so many people in football who will tell you the same - that by jumping in the car, being by yourself and then picking the people you want to speak to, with no interference and no other phones going, you can just concentrate on what you want to. Whereas if you are in your office, you have got this and that going on.

"You might be involved in a really serious debate and then your chairman says he wants to speak to you - then you have to change all of that and go and find out what he wants.

"Whereas when you are in that car and you are by yourself, you have got time to think about everything. I always valued that time and thought it was really important - so it was more beneficial to me as an individual to live away from the club."

He added: "Having my family on the south coast didn't stop me from understanding what the DNA of Stoke City Football Club was. I got to know the area and the fans, and I wanted to give them a team they could identify with.

"Wherever I worked, I never felt I wasn't doing the job I was being paid to do - I always wanted my club to feel like a family.

"I always wanted everyone to feel as though they were part of the family - and the main thing was that everyone pulled and pushed in the right direction."

Pulis, whose last job in management was in 2020 with Sheffield Wednesday, admitted: "I did spend quite a lot of time away from home - my girls would probably tell you I spent more time working away than I should have.

"But that's the way it was for me when I was a manager. You have to get the balance right and I would never have tried to do my job remotely.

"I felt as if I had to be there, taking care of training and everything else during the week. It's about knowing what you think is going to make you successful.

"I don't think any manager would do anything but the right thing to make him and the team successful."

Tony Pulis was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

articles.title: Los 'intocables' de García Plaza
articles.standfirst: Juan Iglesias, Odysseas Vlachodimos, Suazo y Agoumé han jugado todos los minutos
articles.summary: Juan Iglesias, Odysseas Vlachodimos, Suazo y Agoumé han jugado todos los minutos
articles.body: El Sevilla se ha marchado al parón en puestos europeos. El conjunto dirigido por García Plaza ocupa la quinta posición en la tabla de LaLiga EA Sports, con 13 puntos de 21 posibles, gracias a un balance de cuatro victorias (Rayo, Athletic, Valencia y Deportivo), un empate (Espanyol) y dos derrotas (Atlético de Madrid y Barcelona). Un arranque notable que permite a los nervionenses coger aire y seguir insistiendo en los conceptos del técnico madrileño. Al Sevilla le esperan dos salidas consecutivas cuando se reanude la competición (Levante y Real Madrid) y recibirá a Osasuna en el Sánchez-Pizjuán para completar el mes de octubre. El técnico blanquirrojo estará muy pendiente de los jugadores que han sido convocados por sus respectivas selecciones y cruzará los dedos ante la amenaza del siempre temido 'virus FIFA'. Dos de los seis sevillistas que no se detendrán en este paréntesis están en el grupo de los 'intocables' de García Plaza: Odysseas Vlachodimos y Gabriel Suazo. Junto a Juan Iglesias y Agoumé, el guardameta y el lateral zurdo han disputado todos los minutos posibles hasta la fecha. Iglesias, además, fue el protagonista en la victoria frente al Valencia tras marcar el único tanto del encuentro. Tras ellos, turno para la cantera. Miguel Sierra, Castrín y Kike Salas son los siguientes que más tiempo han estado en el terreno de juego. El Sevilla conseguía de nuevo la cesión de Odysseas este verano por parte del Newcastle y el meta ya ha firmado intervenciones de mucho mérito en este primer tramo de la temporada. Ha encajado nueve goles y ha dejado la portería a cero en dos ocasiones (Valencia y Dépor). Suazo, ahora capitán, y Juan Iglesias, en su primer año como sevillista, son los dueños de los laterales del equipo mientras que Agoumé está rindiendo a un nivel sobresaliente. La llegada de Fofana le ha dado alas al francés. García Plaza quiere a todos los jugadores enchufados. 'Unión' y 'familia' son dos palabras que el vestuario tiene interiorizadas y los más veteranos ayudan a los que tienen menos protagonismo. Según el técnico, el próximo Trofeo Antonio Puerta "nos va a venir muy bien para darle minutos a los que menos han tenido". Los nervionenses se medirán al Aston Villa de Unai Emery el próximo viernes 2 de octubre.

articles.title: Raphinha, otra vez de tres en tres para distanciarse en el Pichichi
articles.standfirst: El capitán del Barcelona volvió a liderar el triunfo azulgrana con un nuevo hat-trick ante el Sevilla
articles.summary: El capitán del Barcelona volvió a liderar el triunfo azulgrana con un nuevo hat-trick ante el Sevilla
articles.body: El Barça suma y sigue. Goleando, convenciendo y liderado pro un Raphinha que está, simplemente, espectacular. 12 goles como 12 soles lleva el capitán de los de Flick, quien tras hacerle tres al Racing en la goleada entre semana, volvió a hacer un hat-trick en el Pizjuán para distanciarse aún más en el Pichichi. El atacante barcelonista lidera de forma destacada la tabla con 5 de distancia sobre sus inmediatos perseguidores. Ahí están Lamine, Mbappé y Camello, todos ellos con 7, aunque sólo el atacante rayista vio portería esta jornada previa al parón. En el resto de premios, destaca el empate en el Trofeo Zamora de Radu (Celta) y Sivera (Alavés,), ambos con un coeficiente de 0,86 y con 7 partidos disputados cada uno. articles.title: David Sánchez no compra el discurso arbitral de Mourinho: “Su equipo no juega a nada”
articles.standfirst: El periodista de Radio MARCA criticó en sus 'Picotazos' de 'La Tribu' la queja arbitral del técnico portugués y aseguró que el problema del Real Madrid está en su falta de juego, ambición y presión arriba
articles.summary: El periodista de Radio MARCA criticó en sus 'Picotazos' de 'La Tribu' la queja arbitral del técnico portugués y aseguró que el problema del Real Madrid está en su falta de juego, ambición y presión arriba
articles.body: David Sánchez no compró el discurso arbitral de José Mourinho. En sus Picotazos de La Tribu de Radio MARCA, el periodista fue muy duro con el técnico portugués y con el momento del Real Madrid, después de que el entrenador blanco apuntara a una posible confabulación arbitral para impedir que su equipo gane LaLiga. “Quiero pensar que la afición del Real Madrid es lo suficientemente inteligente como para no comprarle el discurso a José Mourinho de la confabulación arbitral para que el Madrid no gane esta Liga”, arrancó David Sánchez. El periodista admitió que, en caliente, puede entender que una parte del madridismo asuma ese relato durante unas horas, pero no que se mantenga más allá. Para Sánchez, el problema del Real Madrid no está en los árbitros, sino en el fútbol. “A partir de ahí, el madridismo tiene que entender y ver, como ve todo el mundo, que su equipo no juega a nada”, afirmó en La Tribu. El presentador de DSF también cuestionó el impacto de Mourinho en el banquillo. “La que era la solución José Mourinho, no sé si un problema, pero lo que seguro no es de momento es una solución”, señaló. Y comparó el nivel actual con etapas anteriores: “Su equipo juega tan mal como jugaba el de Arbeloa o el de Xabi Alonso”. David Sánchez también puso el foco en la inversión realizada este verano para reforzar la plantilla de Mourinho. A su juicio, que el equipo no haya dado un salto claro en el juego y que el técnico recurra pronto a la queja arbitral deja una imagen preocupante. “Con una inversión importante este verano para reforzar el equipo de José Mourinho, que en la primera vuelta ya tire de fotocopias en color para justificar una derrota, habla muy mal y muy poco del Madrid como institución y de su cuerpo técnico que encabeza José Mourinho”, lanzó. El periodista insistió en que el Real Madrid sigue mostrando carencias muy parecidas a las de cursos anteriores. “El equipo no juega a nada, el equipo no es ofensivo, el equipo no tiene ambición”, afirmó. Sánchez fue más allá y señaló uno de los problemas que, según él, Mourinho tampoco ha conseguido resolver: la implicación defensiva de los jugadores de ataque. “Como se le achacaba a Xabi Alonso y a Arbeloa, este entrenador es incapaz de convencer a los de arriba de que aprieten y de que corran”, apuntó. El Picotazo terminó con una advertencia directa sobre la pelea por el título. Para David Sánchez, si el Real Madrid mantiene esta línea, el campeonato puede quedar encarrilado muy pronto para el Barça. “A este ritmo, sentencia la Liga al Barça a falta de 10 jornadas”, remató el periodista de Radio MARCA. Y cerró con una frase marca de la casa: “Y si no, al tiempo”.

articles.title: Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson's side Republic of Ireland braced for testing Nations League
articles.summary: BBC Sport NI looks at how Republic of Ireland and their opponents - Kosovo, Israel and Austria are shaping up for the Nations League.
articles.body:
The Republic of Ireland's attempt to banish the pain of Prague and their penalty shootout defeat against Czech Republic that cost them a place in the summer's World Cup really begins this month.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side have played four friendlies since that loss, beating Grenada and Qatar and drawing with North Macedonia and Canada, but Thursday's Nations League opener against Kosovo in Pristina will be their first competitive game since that fateful night in March.

It will also feature the return of a more familiar-looking Irish squad after some experimentation in the summer, in a new-look international window, with four games in 12 days.

Hallgrimsson's side will take on Kosovo, Israel twice and Austria in that timeframe and, ahead of a busy spell, BBC Sport NI looks at how the squad and the respective opposition are shaping up.

Coleman not included in Republic of Ireland squad

Hallgrimsson spoke to players individually about Israel games

Uefa rejected request to keep Republic of Ireland and Israel separate - FAI

Collins out and three potential debutants

Hallgrimsson has named a 26-man squad to try and cope with the extra demands of this extended window.

He is without captain Nathan Collins through a calf injury, which is a blow as he has been first-choice when fit to marshal the back three.

Jack Taylor and Mikey Johnston join long-term absentees Evan Ferguson and Josh Cullen, while Oisin McEntee missed out on a first call-up through injury.

Hallgrimsson also confirmed that some players named in the squad are currently nursing injuries or working their way back to full fitness including Jimmy Dunne, Bosun Lawal and Owen Elding, while QPR's Harvey Vale and Hibernian's Jamie McGrath were injured in the warm-up before their clubs' respective games on Saturday and played no part.

Experienced duo Seamus Coleman and Robbie Brady were not considered for selection as they are without clubs.

Sheffield United loanee Liam Kitching has been handed his first call-up while uncapped Cardiff City defender Joel Bagan and Elding of Hibs are in contention to win their first caps.

Hallgrimsson is likely to use if not all, then a large portion of his squad throughout the four games given the schedule and to try to grow some depth, which is much needed in the full-back areas and in midfield.

In-form Parrott's dream start to life in Spain

Few Irish players will be coming into the squad as confident as Troy Parrott, the hero of the previous qualifying campaign, who has taken seamlessly to life in La Liga with Real Betis.

The 24-year-old opened his account for the club by coming off the bench to stab home the winner against Real Madrid earlier this month.

He followed that up with another winning goal a few days later, this time on his Champions League debut to seal a 3-2 victory for Betis away to Lille and he then provided an assist against Getafe.

He has hit the ground running in Spain and will hope to continue his goalscoring exploits on the international stage, where he has firmly established himself as first-choice striker.

Hull City's John Egan and Swansea City's Adam Idah are two other players heading into the break in fine form.

Egan has been a mainstay for the Tigers in their positive start to life back in the Premier League and is pushing to start with Collins out, while Idah has three goals and an assist in eight Championship games for the Swans.

'Our seeding for the Euros depends on the Nations League'

Republic of Ireland's performance in the Nations League will have a lasting impact on their Euro 2028 qualification campaign, so results are important.

Should they finish top of the group, they will earn promotion into League A.

Should they finish second they will have a play-off with a third-placed team from League A to try and win promotion.

More importantly, finishing first or second will also guarantee that the Republic of Ireland will be a pot two side when the draw for the Euro 2028 qualifiers is made in Belfast in December, which, in theory, could present them with a kinder draw.

Should they finish third, they will remain in League B, while if they finish bottom of the group they will have a play-off against a second-placed team from League C, which, if they lost they would then suffer relegation to the third tier of the Nations League.

A third or fourth-placed finish in their group would mean the Republic of Ireland would be placed in pot three for the Euro 2028 qualifiers and they may be paired with two European heavy hitters which could make their path to the tournament much tougher.

A good performance in the Nations League could also offer a route to qualification for the tournament if the Irish fail to qualify automatically.

The best performing teams in the Nations League that do not qualify for the Euros in the qualification campaign will enter play-offs to earn the final qualifying spots for the tournament.

As Hallgrimsson put it when talking through the scenarios: "Our seeding for the Euros depends on the Nations League".

"League A will mean better opponents and would be better financially for FAI [Football Association of Ireland] and there is an escape route to the Euros from the Nations League, so lots of reasons we want to do really well in these Nations League matches," he added.

Kosovo's upheaval, Israel controversy and Austria's new era

Hallgrimsson will hope his side can get off to a positive start in a tricky away test against Kosovo, whose build-up to the game has been far from smooth.

Franco Foda's side, who are in League B for the first time, will be without their captain and one of their best players, Amir Rrahmanhi.

The Napoli defender has decided to retire abruptly from international football because of a fallout with the Football Federation of Kosovo.

The 32-year-old, who has won 66 caps during his 10 years as a Kosovo international, delivered a scathing Instagram statement announcing his decision to step away, accusing the association of "constant, co-ordinated attacks" against him.

In more positive news, Foda has handed a first call-up to exciting Bayern Munich youngster Erblin Osmani, who chose to represent Kosovo earlier this month.

He became Bayern's second youngest ever player in the Bundesliga at 16 years and 306 days when he came on in a 4-0 victory over Union Berlin earlier this year.

The excitement around the potential of the youngster is such that Kosovo's ambassador to Germany, Faruk Ajeti, posted on social media to confirm that Osmani will play for the country after presenting the midfielder with his Kosovo passport, before the player had even announced his decision.

The Republic of Ireland will also face two controversial games against Israel in this window with both being played at neutral venues.

In purely footballing terms, they represent two tough fixtures against a side that featured in League A of the last edition of the Nations League, before factoring in the context around them.

Israel's 'home' game will take place in Hungary on 27 September, and the reverse fixture in Serbia on 4 October.

The FAI confirmed its 'home' tie would be played behind closed doors, while no tickets will be made available for Irish fans for their 'away' game, such is the feeling of unease in the country at the games going ahead.

Hallgrimsson said on Thursday that he spoke to players in his squad individually about the prospect of facing Israel, and "none of us feel comfortable playing in these games" while acknowledging they have to stick together to get through them.

At an extraordinary general meeting in July, delegates backed an FAI motion to proceed with the games amid concerns that boycotting would cause "significant and lasting harm" for the association.

However, the decision has come under increasing pressure, with a 'Stop The Game' campaign launched by Irish Sport for Palestine calling for a boycott and the noise around the two games will undoubtedly get louder and more difficult to manage as they get closer.

In between their games against Israel, Republic of Ireland will have a home game against Austria at the Aviva Stadium.

The Austria side they will face is missing three pillars of the team for the last decade in Marko Arnautovic, David Alaba and Marcel Sabitzer.

Arnautovic, Austria's most capped player and top goal scorer, decided to retire from international football after the country were knocked out of the World Cup at the last 32 stage.

Alaba, Austria's captain at the tournament, is omitted as he is currently without a club after leaving Real Madrid in the summer.

A four-time Champions League winner, he has been blighted by injuries in recent seasons, missing 109 games for club and country over the last three years but he did play all four of Austria's games at the World Cup.

Sabitzer, meanwhile, has decided to take a break from representing his country and will be absent for the entire Nations League campaign.

Given their respective ages, a changing of the guard within the next year felt inevitable and former Manchester United manager Ralf Rangnick has decided to use the Nations League to start bringing through the next generation.

Whether Hallgrimsson will be tempted to do likewise with his squad, with so much riding on his side performing well in these games, will be another intriguing subplot of this testing window on and off the pitch.

articles.title: Ranking every Premier League team's start to the season
articles.summary: Five matches into the league season, which teams in the Premier League have impressed so far and who have disappointed?
articles.body:
There is now a three-week international break with no Premier League games until 10 October.

We are five matches into the league season and there is a long way to go in the campaign, but which teams have impressed so far and who have disappointed?

You can have your say in the comments at the bottom of the page.

Arsenal : Solid start to their title defence until they were ripped apart by Brighton having survived a penalty scare at Sunderland . 7

Aston Villa : Signs they are beginning to move in the right direction after losing so many key players during the transfer window. 6

Bournemouth : If games lasted 80 minutes the Cherries would be near the top of the table. Need to cut out conceding so late. 6

Brentford : Demolished Spurs and Chelsea without fuss during a highly impressive unbeaten start. Can they keep it up and challenge for Europe? 8

Brighton : Kings of entertainment after hitting 16 goals in five top-flight games, including three against champions Arsenal . A joy to watch. 9

Chelsea : After a strong start under Xabi Alonso, the Blues have lost two of their past three - and were picked apart by Brentford . Are they really moving in the right direction? 6

Coventry City : You could hear the sighs of relief in the away end at Nottingham Forest on Saturday. Will Frank Lampard's side kick on after that win? 6

Crystal Palace : Room for improvement after one win and three defeats. 5

Everton : Despite a transfer window to forget, David Moyes has made the Toffees hard to beat. 6

Fulham : Decent draws against Liverpool and Manchester United but need a win. Ipswich (away) followed by Hull (home), Coventry (away) and Crystal Palace (home) offer hope when they return from the international break. 5

Hull City : To have eight points from a tough opening five fixtures is an excellent return, including beating Manchester United and drawing with Aston Villa and Chelsea . 8

Ipswich Town : Defensively vulnerable but two late winners, against Sunderland and Crystal Palace , have earned them six points and shown their fighting spirit. 5

Leeds United : Fifth in the league, unbeaten and with the joint-best defensive record. They showed what they are capable of with a superb 4-1 win over Newcastle . 7

Liverpool : Unbeaten but have been far from their best. Three clean sheets in their past three games, but more is expected from Andoni Iraola's side. 6

Manchester City : Five league games, five victories. Managed to win at Manchester United despite going down to 10 men midway through the first half. With Erling Haaland already top scorer, City fans will expect a real push to win the league. 9

Manchester United : Disappointing performances to lose at Hull and draw at a Fulham side who were bottom of the league. Their only win so far came against Ipswich and they were denied a victory at Everton by a late equaliser. 4

Newcastle United : A mixed bag under new manager Matthias Jaissle. They impressed in a draw against Liverpool , won comfortably at Tottenham , but were also terrible in a loss at Leeds , although they responded well to beat Hull. 6

Nottingham Forest : Their best results have come away, drawing at Liverpool and winning at Aston Villa . But their home form will be a huge worry - yet to score a goal and with only one point from three matches at the City Ground. 5

Sunderland : After coming seventh in 2025-26, Sunderland fans will have wanted a better start to this season. The Black Cats gave good accounts of themselves against Arsenal and Manchester City , but lost both matches. 5

Tottenham Hotspur : After spending more than £300m in the summer, Spurs have been poor, failing to score in their opening four league matches. Supporters will be demanding an instant improvement after the international break. 2

articles.title: Un empate agridulce que no empaña el gran inicio de temporada del Betis
articles.standfirst: Los verdiblancos se marchan a la fecha FIFA de septiembre con 16 puntos de 21 posibles
articles.summary: Los verdiblancos se marchan a la fecha FIFA de septiembre con 16 puntos de 21 posibles
articles.body: El gol del empate del Deportivo de la Coruña ayer en Riazor, cuando el partido se aproximaba al minuto 90, dejó al Betis sin una victoria que prácticamente acariciaba. Los verdiblancos habían tenido oportunidades para sentenciar el partido en la segunda parte, tras el gol del Cucho que abrió el marcador en el primer acto, pero al final dejaron escapar dos puntos, pecando de cierto conformismo o, tal vez, sufriendo en las piernas la carga de minutos con tres encuentros en apenas seis días, un calendario incomprensible. Lo cierto es que el gol de Villares, que premió la insistencia y el empuje del conjunto gallego en la segunda parte, dejó un sabor agridulce en la expedición heliopolitana antes de la fecha FIFA de selecciones que arranca hoy. Una pequeña decepción que, en cualquier caso, no debe empañar el sensacional arranque de temporada de un Betis que sólo ha perdido un partido de los ocho que ha disputado desde que arrancó la competición el pasado mes de agosto entre Liga y Champions. "Firmábamos un 16 de 21 para empezar", sentenció Pellegrini. Con el punto de Riazor, lo verdiblancos igualan el mejor arranque liguero de su historia desde que las victorias suman tres puntos. Un registro que les permite irse al parón en puestos Champions en la clasificación, terceros en la tabla empatados a puntos con el Atlético de Madrid que es segundo por diferencia general de goles, por delante incluso del Real Madrid, al que superaron hace un par de semanas en La Cartuja. Además, aventajan en ocho puntos a Villarreal y Athletic, y nueve a Celta y Real Sociedad, sus teóricos rivales directos en la lucha por Europa. El volumen rematador que habían mostrado los de Pellegrini en sus últimos partidos, ante el Deportivo no fue tal. De hecho, quien superó los 20 disparos fue el conjunto gallego, frenado por otra gran actuación de Álvaro Valles. El plan de intentar defenderse en la segunda parte con balón y posesiones largas en lugar de ir a rematar el resultado le terminó pasando factura al Betis. Pero tanto su técnico como el vestuario hicieron un balance positivo de este primer tramo de temporada, al que se van con el único borrón de lo sucedido en el Ciudad de Valencia. A la vuelta de los partidos internacionales, los verdiblancos tendrán una oportunidad de oro de seguir dando pasos adelante hacia sus objetivos con cuatro partidos seguidos en casa: dos de Liga, ante Osasuna, que llega tras un arranque de curso repleto de dudas, y frente al líder, el Barcelona, que ya está avisado de lo que el Betis es capaz en La Cartuja; los otros dos encuentros pueden resultar determinantes para saber si el acceso a las rondas eliminatorias de la Champions es posible por primera vez en su historia para los de Pellegrini. El Betis arrancó su participación en la máxima competición continental remontando por dos veces un marcador adverso en Francia frente al Lille para sumar sus primeros tres puntos. En octubre recibirá en casa al Oporto, un adversario de mucho nivel, y al Feyenoord, al que ya ganó en enero en la fase de liga de la Europa League. Seis puntos vitales con los que dar un paso de gigante para estar en el sorteo de los cruces y seguir soñando en el Viejo Continente... pero sin descuidar su camino casi inmaculado en LaLiga, pese al sabor agridulce del empate de Riazor.

articles.title: England squad: Morgan Gibbs-White set to replace Cole Palmer for Nations League games
articles.summary: Morgan Gibbs-White is in line for an England recall to replace Cole Palmer, who is set to withdraw from the squad because of a minor injury.
articles.body:
Morgan Gibbs-White is in line for an England recall to replace Cole Palmer, who is set to withdraw from the squad because of a minor injury.

Nottingham Forest midfielder Gibbs-White missed out on selection in the initial squad for the upcoming Nations League matches, but is set to be called up.

Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel admitted on Friday that Gibbs-White was close to making the cut and the 26-year-old is now expected to replace Chelsea 's Palmer.

Palmer, 24, had been recalled by Tuchel after being controversially left out of England's World Cup squad.

Tuchel previously said Palmer had a "point to prove" and needed "to step up" to "keep his shirt and justify the nomination".

However, the Blues forward will now miss the extended international break in which England play four games.

The Three Lions face World Cup winners Spain at Wembley on Saturday, 26 September, then travel to the Czech Republic (29 September) and Croatia (3 October) before hosting the Czechs on 6 October.

Manchester United duo Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo are also both thought to be injury doubts for England.

They are being assessed by their club after being taken off in the closing stages of Sunday's 1-1 draw at Fulham .

If Mainoo withdraws, it is understood Everton midfielder James Garner - who made his senior England debut in March but was not selected for the World Cup - is a strong option to replace him.

Tuchel recalls Alexander-Arnold and Palmer with warning

How does the Nations League work and who is in each league?

Palmer's withdrawal comes after he played the full game for Chelsea in their 3-0 defeat at Brentford on Friday.

Following a summer off after missing out on World Cup selection, he has started six of Chelsea 's seven games and played the full 90 minutes in five of them - scoring four goals and providing two assists.

Palmer, who last played for England in their 1-0 friendly defeat by Japan in March, was hampered by a recurring groin injury in 2025-26, which Chelsea had to manage.

Gibbs-White made his most recent England appearance in a 3-0 friendly win against Wales in October 2025.

He has one goal and two assists from Forest's five league games this season.

articles.title: "Es el mayor escándalo arbitral en un partido de LaLiga"
articles.standfirst: Javier Tintó carga contra la actuación arbitral en el derbi y reclama que el Atlético debió acabar con nueve jugadores
articles.summary: Javier Tintó carga contra la actuación arbitral en el derbi y reclama que el Atlético debió acabar con nueve jugadores
articles.body: Javier Tintó, Fernando Polo, Nacho Labarga, Antonio Sanz, Jorge Liaño y Pepe Pasqués han sido los tertulianos de este lunes en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar la victoria del Atlético de Madrid en el derbi, la polémica arbitral y las declaraciones de Mourinho contra el CTA. Javier Tintó. "Es el mayor escándalo arbitral que he visto en un partido de LaLiga española. ¿Cuándo has visto en el minuto 40 dos rojas no pitadas? El partido cambia ahí. En el minuto 40, el Atleti se tiene que quedar con 9. Un 11 contra 9 es una goleada del Madrid. Es un escándalo. Es un atraco a mano armada". Fernando Polo. "No puede ser que por una designación, que se hace con buena intención y que no es la primera vez que se hace, se abra una causa general contra el arbitraje después de siete jornadas y antes del parón liguero porque el Madrid pierde un partido. Eso lo que pretendía Mourinho. ¿Ahora en qué estamos? ¿En cómo juega el Madrid o en que hay una conspiración arbitral?". Nacho Labarga. "Lo de Ortiz Arias fue una designación arriesgada. Se le quedó un poquito grande el partido, está completamente presionado, no está a la altura del partido. El Madrid necesitaba un electroshock de Mourinho y no se lo está dando". Antonio Sanz. "Simeone le da un baño a Mourinho. El problema del Madrid es este Barça. Lleva cuatro entrenadores mientras el Barça ha tenido uno. La aplastante situación deportiva del Barça hace mucho daño al Madrid". Jorge Liaño. "El Madrid no juega un pimiento al fútbol, no juega a nada. Falta fútbol en todo el equipo. Falta una idea, un estilo y sobran excusas. Lo de los árbitros son excusas". Pepe Pasqués. "En ocho partidos el Madrid fue a dos campos difíciles y perdió los dos, y no solucionó los problemas que tiene en el campo de juego desde temporadas anteriores. ¿La rueda de prensa? Le dieron la excusa necesaria. El equipo juega mal, no juega a nada".
